title: The Kingdom Divided

questions.question: Where did all Israel go to make Rehoboam king?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:1 (ESV): "Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king."

questions.question: Whose counsel did Rehoboam reject?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:8 (ESV): "But he abandoned the counsel that the old men gave him..."

questions.question: What did the young men advise Rehoboam to say?
options: My little finger is thicker than my father's thighs
questions.correctAnswer: My little finger is thicker than my father's thighs
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:10 (ESV): "...Thus shall you speak to them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's thighs.'"

questions.question: Which tribe remained loyal to the house of David?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:20 (ESV): "...There was none that followed the house of David but the tribe of Judah only."

questions.question: What did Jeroboam make to keep people from going to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:28 (ESV): "So the king took counsel and made two calves of gold..."

questions.question: Where did Jeroboam place the golden calves?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:29 (ESV): "And he set one in Bethel, and the other he put in Dan."

questions.question: Who did Rehoboam send to call Israel, who was then stoned?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:18 (ESV): "Then King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was taskmaster over the forced labor, and all Israel stoned him..."

questions.question: Who forbade Rehoboam from fighting against Israel?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:22 (ESV): "But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God..."

questions.question: What did Jeroboam say to the people about the calves?
options: Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:28 (ESV): "...And he said to the people... 'Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.'"

questions.question: What cities did Jeroboam build/fortify?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:25 (ESV): "Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim... and went out from there and built Penuel."

questions.question: From whom did Jeroboam appoint priests?
options: From among all the people, who were not of the Levites
questions.correctAnswer: From among all the people, who were not of the Levites
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:31 (ESV): "...and he appointed priests from among all the people, who were not of the Levites."

questions.question: When did Jeroboam ordain a feast to mimic the one in Judah?
options: The fifteenth day of the eighth month
The fourteenth day of the first month
The tenth day of the seventh month
The first day of the year
questions.correctAnswer: The fifteenth day of the eighth month
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:32 (ESV): "And Jeroboam appointed a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month like the feast that was in Judah..."

questions.question: To where did Rehoboam flee?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:18 (ESV): "...King Rehoboam hurried to mount his chariot to flee to Jerusalem."

questions.question: What was the complaint of the people to Rehoboam?
options: Your father made our yoke heavy
questions.correctAnswer: Your father made our yoke heavy
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:4 (ESV): "Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service..."

questions.question: Why did the king not listen to the people according to verse 15?
options: It was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: It was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:15 (ESV): "So the king did not listen to the people, for it was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD..."

key_verse_text: So the king took counsel and made two calves of gold. And he said to the people, “You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.” (ESV)
